{{Short description|Axiomatic system in mathematics}}
In mathematics, a '''quaternionic structure''' or {{math|'''''Q'''''}}'''-structure''' is an axiomatic system that abstracts the concept of a [[quaternion algebra]] over a [[field (algebra)|field]].

A ''quaternionic structure'' is a triple {{math|(''G'', ''Q'', ''q'')}} where {{math|''G''}} is an [[elementary abelian group]] of [[exponent (group theory)|exponent]] {{math|2}} with a distinguished element {{math|−1}}, {{math|''Q''}} is a [[pointed set]] with distinguished element {{math|1}}, and {{math|''q''}} is a symmetric [[surjection]] {{math|''G''×''G'' → ''Q''}} satisfying axioms

:<math>\begin{align}\text{1.} \quad &q(a,(-1)a) = 1,\\
\text{2.} \quad &q(a,b) = q(a,c) \Leftrightarrow q(a,bc) = 1,\\
\text{3.} \quad &q(a,b) = q(c,d) \Rightarrow \exists x\mid q(a,b) = q(a,x), q(c,d) = q(c,x)\end{align}.</math>

Every field {{math|''F''}} gives rise to a {{math|''Q''}}-structure by taking {{math|''G''}} to be {{math|''F''<sup>∗</sup>/''F''<sup>∗2</sup>}}, {{math|''Q''}} the set of [[Brauer class]]es of quaternion algebras in the [[Brauer group]] of {{math|''F''}} with the [[split quaternion algebra]] as distinguished element and {{math|''q''(''a'',''b'')}} the quaternion algebra {{math|(''a'',''b'')<sub>''F''</sub>}}.
